prompt: A flat layered paper-cut collage in a strict handcraft design system: everything is cut from colored cardstock and hanji paper with perfectly clean cut edges — NO outline of any kind on any piece: no bright edge line, no white edge, no dark contour line. Each object is built from two to five completely flat die-cut pieces layered ON THE OBJECT ITSELF — its own silhouette, a main color piece, one or two detail pieces and a highlight piece — the object is never placed on a base, platform, pedestal, plinth or pile of paper sheets; Every upper piece sits slightly RAISED above the piece beneath it, so along EVERY boundary where two different colors meet, the upper piece casts a soft narrow warm dark-brown shadow down onto the lower piece — a gentle embossed paper relief wherever two colors touch, and this relief shadow is the ONLY depth cue. Cut economy: every scissor cut is purposeful and confident — a shape that is straight in the real object is cut with a clean STRAIGHT edge, and curves appear ONLY where the real object is actually curved. No decorative wavy edges, no bumpy wobbly outlines, no gratuitous scalloping on untextured surfaces; a rectangular block is cut as a plain rectangle, though corners may be gently ROUNDED — softly rounding a corner is natural scissor work. Shapes stay simple and chunky, no detail finer than real scissors could cut. Scalloped repeat patterns for textures like straw or waves, cut big and loose. Strictly straight-on orthographic front view, zero perspective. No volume, no curvature, no folded paper, no sculpting. Real-scissors discipline: every piece is a shape that could actually be cut with scissors from a single sheet of colored paper. EACH PIECE IS EXACTLY ONE SOLID FLAT COLOR — no gradient, no shading, no airbrush, no painted detail inside a piece; every color change is a separate stacked paper piece, even a thin line is its own paper strip. ALL pieces share one identical fine colored-paper texture. All shadows are neutral warm dark-brown paper shadows, never colored. Palette: deep indigo #1F2A56, midnight navy #16204a, lavender dusk #8B7BB8 (sea and moonlit ridges ONLY), snow white #F4F6FA, paper cream #F6ECD8, straw gold #D9A94E, ember amber #F2B366, bark brown #6B4A32. Cold winter moonlit night mood with warm amber window lights. A small distant Korean village: three or four small thatched-roof houses as flat dark indigo-brown paper silhouettes with tiny warm amber window dots, and a soft row of dark indigo pine tree silhouettes behind them, sitting on a gentle flat paper hill line. The element is shown whole and uncropped, centered, straight-on. Isolated on a plain solid flat lime green (#7CFC00) background, nothing else. The paper pieces cast NO shadow onto the lime area: no drop shadow, no ground shadow, no backing shape — only tiny shallow shadows between their own stacked pieces. Do NOT paint any glow, halo, light spill, shadow or color onto the lime background; the lime stays one perfectly flat uniform color right up to the paper edges. No text, no watermark.

Each object is built from two to five completely flat die-cut pieces layered ON THE OBJECT ITSELF — its own silhouette, a main color piece, one or two detail pieces and a highlight piece — the object is never placed on a base, platform, pedestal, plinth or pile of paper sheets; Every upper piece sits slightly RAISED above the piece beneath it, so along EVERY boundary where two different colors meet, the upper piece casts a soft narrow warm dark-brown shadow down onto the lower piece — a gentle embossed paper relief wherever two colors touch, and this relief shadow is the ONLY depth cue. Cut economy: every scissor cut is purposeful and confident — a shape that is straight in the real object is cut with a clean STRAIGHT edge, and curves appear ONLY where the real object is actually curved. No decorative wavy edges, no bumpy wobbly outlines, no gratuitous scalloping on untextured surfaces; a rectangular block is cut as a plain rectangle, though corners may be gently ROUNDED — softly rounding a corner is natural scissor work. Shapes stay simple and chunky, no detail finer than real scissors could cut. Scalloped repeat patterns for textures like straw or waves, cut big and loose. Strictly straight-on orthographic front view, zero perspective. No volume, no curvature, no folded paper, no sculpting. Real-scissors discipline: every piece is a shape that could actually be cut with scissors from a single sheet of colored paper. EACH PIECE IS EXACTLY ONE SOLID FLAT COLOR — no gradient, no shading, no airbrush, no painted detail inside a piece; every color change is a separate stacked paper piece, even a thin line is its own paper strip. ALL pieces share one identical fine colored-paper texture. All shadows are neutral warm dark-brown paper shadows, never colored. Palette: paper cream #F6ECD8 clay wall, warm ochre, bark brown #6B4A32 wood, deep shadow brown #2E241C, ember amber #F2B366 fire light, straw gold #D9A94E. Dark winter night kitchen lit warmly by the hearth fire. A wide flat strip of dark packed-earth kitchen floor with a slightly lighter front step edge (bongdang), one clear narrow crack in the middle of the floor, and a few flat scattered straw bits. A plain horizontal strip, much wider than tall. The element is shown whole and uncropped, centered, straight-on. Isolated on a plain solid flat lime green (#7CFC00) background, nothing else. The paper pieces cast NO shadow onto the lime area: no drop shadow, no ground shadow, no backing shape — only tiny shallow shadows between their own stacked pieces. Do NOT paint any glow, halo, light spill, shadow or color onto the lime background; the lime stays one perfectly flat uniform color right up to the paper edges. No text, no watermark.
